modules.module_title: Fundamentals of CNC Milling Machine Programming — Core Assessment Criteria

pcs.pc_description: follow standard operating procedures (SOPs)

• read, interpret and follow the information on written job instructions, specifications, SOPs, part • information, CNC milling process plan/sheet, charts, lists, drawings and other applicable reference • documents to obtain job requirements, tasks and relevant information
• determine the machining operations and processing sequence to be performed on the CNC milling • machine through the available documents and information

• interpret information such as cutting parameters, revolutions per minute (RPM), feed speed • (mm/min), axial depth of cut, and radial depth of cut, etc. from the sketches, job sheets, process • plan/sheet etc.

• identify the programming method, dimensions, material requirements, cutting tool type, clamping • and positioning method, workholding device, tool requirements from the tooling layout, cutting • process etc. from the available documents and information and assess their suitability
check the process sheet and match it with the received drawings and other specifications
clarify relevant specifications and procedures from relevant person
select appropriate CNC program elements for milling machine controller
• coordinate with the relevant personnel to report and rectify incorrect and inconsistent information in • job specification documents
interpret engineering drawings to define milling machine function and tool path geometry
calculate coordinates for tool path or milling functions, as required
write program in standard code format in accordance with SOPs

• write the CNC program with commands for tool motions, spindle motions, miscellaneous functions • and tool change, in syntax corresponding to the milling machine and control system on which the • component will be machined

• define the programming coordinate system, fully consider factors such as characteristics of the • processed material, cutting characteristics of the milling tool, and material condition of the part that • need to be removed in the program

• define processing method, process parameters (including margin, feed speed and processing tool • path span, etc.) and auxiliary attributes (including tool setting point, safety surface, milling machine • tool attributes, etc.) in the program
• follow the appropriate method for creating the CNC program, such as text editor or Computer-Aided • Manufacturing (CAM) software or controllers on machine
• ensure the part program is efficient and results in minimal cycle time, with optimal cutting • parameters and no unnecessary tool motions
select advanced operations using canned cycles and sub-routines and apply
• transfer the program to the milling machine by entering it in the console or transmitting it through a • wired link or a data transfer device
use the part program in single block mode and check the condition of the tool after each operation
check the sequence of the program as per the process sheet
• check the annotation information, selection of the processing method, tool size information, tool • compensation information etc. in the CNC milling processing program is correct
check for over-cutting, under-cutting or collision interference in the CNC milling program
• check the CNC milling program, spindle speed and feed speed match the current CNC milling machine • tool
• follow the recommended procedures for calling up the program and dealing with any error messages • or faults
• follow the approved procedures to resolve problems encountered with the programming, loading and • editing activities
use the appropriate storage medium such as a computer hard disk for saving the proven program
• produce operation sheets to specification in accordance with SOPs which includes appropriate, where • required
• select and prepare the appropriate tools and equipment for testing and proving the program, • ensuring they are not worn-out or damaged
ensure all the measuring equipment are calibrated and approved for use
pre-set the tooling appropriately using setting jigs/fixtures
mount tools in the correct positions in the tool turret or magazine
check the tools are mounted in positions corresponding to the tool numbers in the part program
operate milling machine in manual mode to test and prove program
cut a trial part using single block run, dry run and feed, and speed override controls
edit program, if necessary to adjust operation, as required
follow the recommended practices to resolve error messages and faults on the program or equipment
check components to conform to specification
• ensure the trial part conforms to drawing specifications in terms of dimensions, surface finishes and • geometrical parameters such as concentricity, parallelism, runout, etc.
prepare and verify all technical documents for CNC programs
